experiment: EM2 — emergence at the simple-tissue level: a squid giant axon built from its measured membrane elements
principle: Elements and constants are observations (Hodgkin & Huxley 1952, J. Physiol. 117:500): Na, K and leak conductances with their measured voltage- and time-dependence, membrane capacitance, axoplasm resistivity, axon radius. The action potential and its conduction velocity are NOT set; they must emerge. No constant is tuned to the outputs.

constants_observed.rate_functions: HH 1952 alpha/beta at 6.3 C with temperature factor phi = 3^((T-6.3)/10)

observations_to_compare.O1: measured conduction velocity 21.2 m/s at 18.5 C on this axon (HH 1952); HH's own hand computation gave 18.8 m/s
observations_to_compare.O2: action potential amplitude ~100-110 mV from rest (overshoot of ~+40 mV above zero on a -65 mV rest), duration ~1-2 ms at 18.5 C
observations_to_compare.O3: a refractory period follows each spike: a second equal stimulus a few ms later fails

predictions.P1_velocity: emergent conduction velocity within 15% of the measured 21.2 m/s
predictions.P2_amplitude: emergent spike amplitude 90-120 mV from rest
predictions.P3_all_or_none: the space-clamped membrane shows a threshold: stimuli below it give < 10 mV, above it a full spike (> 80 mV)
predictions.P4_refractory: a second threshold-plus stimulus 2 ms after the first (at 18.5 C) fails to give a full spike, and one 15 ms later succeeds
